statement: X06.2's code KG indexer chose git2 (libgit2 bindings) over gix for read-only git metadata (HEAD commit, last-commit-per-path, change-count-per-path), and chose tree-sitter 0.24 + tree-sitter-rust/tree-sitter-typescript/tree-sitter-python 0.23.x as the parsing layer, added directly to crates/enforcer-memory/Cargo.toml (no workspace.dependencies entry needed -- crates in this workspace commonly declare their own non-workspace deps per crates/enforcer-lang-ts/Cargo.toml's pattern).
why: git2 is the more battle-tested, synchronous, blocking-call-friendly surface for exactly the narrow read-only revwalk/diff queries this indexer needs; gix's async/pure-Rust selling points are not needed for a local, synchronous, read-only indexer, and gix's porcelain surface for per-path history is less complete. TypeScript's grammar is a strict superset of JavaScript syntax for everything the extractor cares about (functions, classes, interfaces, imports, calls, route decorators), so one grammar crate covers both required languages instead of two.
howToApply: Any future x06 subpack (X06.3 graph algorithms, X06.4 full-text/vector) that needs git metadata should reuse crate::git::GitMetadata rather than re-wrapping git2 or introducing gix; any future language addition should follow the languages/<lang>.rs + one parsers::parse_file dispatch-arm pattern already established for rust/typescript/python.

statement: On this Windows/MSVC toolchain, git2's libgit2-sys crate links successfully but FAILS AT LINK TIME (LNK2019, ~19 unresolved externals: OpenProcessToken, CheckTokenMembership, CopySid, RegOpenKeyExW, CryptAcquireContextA, etc.) unless the consuming crate supplies advapi32 as an extra link-lib -- libgit2-sys's own build.rs only emits winhttp/rpcrt4/ole32/crypt32/secur32 for target_os=windows, which is missing the SID/registry/CryptoAPI functions libgit2's fs_path.c/sysdir.c/rand.c actually call.
why: cargo build -p enforcer-memory succeeded (compiling is not linking), but cargo test -p enforcer-memory failed at the final executable-link step for every test binary, which would have looked like a mysterious, crate-unrelated linker failure if not traced back to libgit2-sys's incomplete Windows link-lib list.
howToApply: Any crate in this workspace that adds a direct or transitive dependency on git2 on Windows/MSVC must ship a build.rs that does `println!("cargo:rustc-link-lib=advapi32")` when CARGO_CFG_TARGET_OS==windows -- crates/enforcer-memory/build.rs is the reference implementation. This is a deviation from the strict file-claim list for X06.2 (build.rs was not pre-listed) but was required for the crate to link at all once git2 was added; flagged explicitly in the lane's final report rather than silently added.

evidence.ref: crates/enforcer-memory/build.rs; linker output LNK2019 x19 unresolved externals in libgit2_sys fs_path.o/sysdir.o/win32.o/rand.o before the fix

statement: X06.2's CodeGraph::index_repository deliberately diverges from the codebase-memory-mcp (C) baseline's incremental-indexing pattern studied during the research pass: codebase-memory-mcp's pipeline_incremental.c classifies files as changed/unchanged via mtime+size (not content hash) and, for deleted files, relies on SQLite ON DELETE CASCADE to remove the old nodes outright -- it does not create an explicit tombstone node. X06.2 instead uses a SHA-256 content hash for the unchanged-file skip (more robust than mtime+size against touch-without-edit and across checkouts/clones) and creates an explicit CodeNode::Tombstone node retaining rel_path/last_commit/change_count/prior_chunk_ids for every deleted file, per the workpack's literal 'Deleted files get tombstones' + 'retain file history summary' hard requirements.
why: The owner's design-inputs doc (MEMORY_RETRIEVAL_DESIGN_INPUTS.md) explicitly authorizes borrowing from codebase-memory-mcp as a baseline while still building enforcer's own KG model on top -- the workpack text for X06.2 is more specific than the C baseline on this exact point (explicit tombstones + history retention), so the workpack's explicit text wins.
howToApply: Do not 'fix' CodeGraph to match codebase-memory-mcp's cascade-delete behavior -- the tombstone-retention design is intentional and tested (deleted_file_gets_tombstone_not_silently_dropped in both crates/enforcer-memory/src/code_graph.rs and tests/code_graph_indexer.rs).

evidence.ref: codebase-memory-mcp src/pipeline/pipeline_incremental.c (mtime+size classify, cascade-delete, studied in scratchpad research clone, not vendored into this repo) vs crates/enforcer-memory/src/code_graph.rs CodeGraph::index_repository
